# dsh-cbm-autorefresh

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that keeps
codebase-memory indexes fresh **per Session**.

Harness opens one MCP connection for the whole app, so `codebase-memory` never learns which
workspac

e a Session is actually working in — every project reports
`watch.reason: not_session_project` and n
othing auto-refreshes. This plugin closes that gap:

- on `session/created`, it refreshes the index of **that Session's own working directory**;
- on `wo

rking-directory/change`, it refreshes the **new** directory instead;
- when the plugin itself (re)lo
ads, it catches up on the Sessions that already exist.

Each refresh is one or more short-lived CLI calls (1–3 s when nothing changed). All heavy
indexing h

appens inside codebase-memory's shared daemon, so the plugin never keeps a background
process alive:
N Sessions do **not** mean N resident processes.

## Behaviour and limits
| Situation | Result |

| Session starts in an indexed repo | index refreshed (≈1–3 s when unchanged) |
| Session switches t

o another indexed repo | that repo's index refreshed |
| Repo not indexed yet | skipped and logged —

first indexing stays a deliberate act |
| Not a git working directory | skipped and logged |
| Same

directory within `minIntervalMs` | skipped (throttled) |
| Same repo already refreshing | skipped (

n `minIntervalMs` | skipped (throttled) |
| Same repo already refreshing | skipped (single-flight) |
Known limits:

- the plugin does not create indexes, it only refreshes existing ones;
- a Session that edits a lot

without starting a new turn or changing directory stays refreshed
at session start only — raise the

triggers yourself if you need more;
- requires `codebase-memory-mcp` on the machine (the `binary` co
nfig or `$CBM_BIN`).
